body:
This issue is revealed because of the #118080 optimisation, but I believe that the root cause (and fix) is in CharacterBody (not RigidBody sync, which is a hot path).

I have modified the MRP to demonstrate that the problem doesn't happen when you are pinned to a Rigid Body:
[bug_hunt_pin_joint_2d_test_1_rigid.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31225212/bug_hunt_pin_joint_2d_test_1_rigid.zip)

I suspect CharacterBody is not synching its transform changes to children the way it should.

I would argue the fundamental problem here is the childing of a `RigidBody2D` to another moving node in the first place, same ~~as #121038 and~~ #120671. This is known to be problematic for several reasons and ideally shouldn't be done. It's somewhat vaguely mentioned in [the documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_rigidbody2d.html#description) for `RigidBody2D` already:

> Note: Changing the 2D transform [...] of a RigidBody2D very often may lead to some unpredictable behaviors. This also happens when a RigidBody2D is the descendant of a constantly moving node, like another RigidBody2D, as that will cause its global transform to be set whenever its ancestor moves.

You get all kinds of weird feedback loops when you continuously transform simulated bodies like this, that might only be apparent under certain circumstances, and you just generally end up fighting the physics engine.

If you do still want to have the `RigidBody2D` be childed to the node it's jointed to, then adding this script to the `RigidBody2D` should help you achieve that, albeit in a somewhat hacky way:

```gdscript
extends RigidBody2D

func _detach_from_parent() -> void:
	await get_tree().physics_frame
	await get_tree().physics_frame
	top_level = true

func _ready() -> void:
	_detach_from_parent()
```

Basically, just use `top_level`, so that the `RigidBody2D` isn't affected by its parent at all once the physics simulation gets going.

The double `await` is the hacky part obviously, but without it you'll find the `RigidBody2D` flying all the way from `[0, 0]` to where it ought to be when you start the scene. The double `await` allows for one physics flush+process+step to happen, which solves that for reasons I honestly can't remember right now. Possibly related to the deferred transformations that kinematic bodies go through.

---

With all that said, I haven't looked into this MRP in-depth yet, but it likely happened to work-ish prior to #118080 because of the `CanvasItem::_notify_transform` bug I talked about [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/120671#issuecomment-4983705329). However, unlike #121038 and #120671 this is obviously all happening during physics processing, and not regular/idle processing, so there might be something else going on that warrants fixing.

As for #122553, I assume that's effectively just a revert of #118080, since `get_parent_item()` will presumably be a valid reference for any `RigidBody2D`?

I still don't think reverting #118080 is the right move here, but it might be time to start thinking about adding a warning for continuous transforming of a `RigidBody*D`, as discussed in #120671. This has been an issue for years at this point, long before #118080.

Thanks for the feedback. This isn't a full revert of #118080, since root and top-level bodies still keep the optimization, but I understand that it is broad for parented `RigidBody2D` nodes. Since you've assigned yourself the issue, I'll leave the deeper investigation to you.
